ordinance_area_text: (2) Any public park owned or operated by the County, or by any authority or local governmental entity created or controlled by the County;
method: Loudoun County official GIS layer COL/PRCSbuildings/MapServer/1 'Parks and Recreation Areas' (140 polygons). Kept features whose PR_LMIS_OWN owner is Loudoun County (any spelling, incl. School Board) or an authority (Northern Virginia Regional Park Authority; Loudoun County Sanitation Authority/Loudoun Water for Beaverdam Reservoir). Dropped libraries (PR_TYPE 'LB'), status 'FUT' (future) parks, and parks owned by towns (Leesburg, Round Hill, Hamilton, Purcellville), NPS, the state (Sweet Run SP, DGIF boat launch) or private/HOA bodies. Added 2 county parcels from COL/CountyOwnedLeased ('Part of Trailside Park', 'Arcola Community Center'). Dissolved by name.
notes: 90 named parks. 684.04 is a firearm POSSESSION ban (which in practice bars firearm hunting); archery is not addressed by this section. Each feature carries an 'operator' property: 'Loudoun County', 'NVRPA' (e.g. Algonkian, Temple Hall, Balls Bluff, Red Rock, W&OD Trail), or Loudoun Water/NVRPA (Beaverdam Reservoir). Including NVRPA parks is an interpretation: NVRPA is a multi-jurisdiction authority Loudoun belongs to, not one Loudoun controls by itself. Excluded but worth knowing: Leesburg/Round Hill/Hamilton/Purcellville town parks (town rules apply), Morven Park, Broadlands Nature Center, Rust Sanctuary, Middleburg Community Center, and future/unopened county parks (Goose Creek Pointe, Ashburn Farm, Avonlea Reserve, Lerner, Western Loudoun Rec Center, Springdale Regional Park). DCR lists some older park polygons (Lansdowne Sports, Evergreen Conservancy, Harper, Cardinal Park, Broadlands Parcel, Round Hill CC) that are missing from the county's current layer; they were not added. Separately, 684.03(c) bans discharge within 100 yd of any public park; that buffer is not modeled here.
recovered: Recovered 2026-11 from public/data/local-areas.geojson (the original source files were lost); geometry carries that layer's 30% simplification.
